description: Explore this repository codebase, optionally grounded in a specific GitHub issue or Jira ticket used as the task to investigate, and detect the programming language(s) and framework(s) in play — including Vite+React, Angular CLI, Hilla (Spring Boot + Vaadin + Hilla), Kotlin Spring Boot, Quarkus (Java or Kotlin), NestJS, Next.js, PHP (Laravel, WordPress plugin/theme, PrestaShop module, plain Composer package), Python (FastAPI, Django, plain package), React Native (Expo vs. bare React Native CLI/Metro toolchain), Ionic/Capacitor, Kotlin Multiplatform (Compose Multiplatform vs. native UI), Android (library vs. application, Compose), SwiftPM/Xcode/XcodeGen/Tuist stacks, macOS desktop apps (SwiftUI vs. AppKit, MVVM vs. MVC), Windows desktop apps on .NET (WPF, WinUI 3, Windows Forms; MVVM vs. MVC), Rust and Go projects, and command-line tools (Rust clap/Ratatui, Go Cobra/Bubble Tea, Swift ArgumentParser, .NET System.CommandLine) — both in the existing codebase and in the requested change, and reports a normalized `Project type:` line for downstream bootstrap tooling — plus whether Antora documentation exists and where, which platform hosts the repository (GitHub, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, or TFS), and whether a `.archive/` directory holds implementation plans from previously resolved tasks that resemble the current one. Works even when the current working directory isn't a git repository at all — it warns the user that git-remote-dependent tooling (e.g. `gh` inferring an owner/repo, `git log` history) won't work, then keeps going with whatever sources don't need one: a Jira ticket, a connected documentation MCP, and any files actually present in the working directory. Invoke as `/iru-explore <ticket-id>` where `<ticket-id>` is either a GitHub issue ID (e.g. `42`) or a Jira key (e.g. `PROJ-123`) — the skill auto-detects which. If invoked as `/iru-explore` with no argument, ask the user for a ticket ID; if they decline or give none, just explore the current codebase. Looks up GitHub issues with the `gh` CLI (or GitHub MCP tools if `gh` is unavailable) and Jira tickets via any connected Jira MCP tools — for a Jira ticket, also fetches its epic and any linked/related tickets (one hop out), and downloads and reads any `implementation_plan_*.md` attached to the ticket, its epic, or its linked tickets (the naming convention `iru-code`/`iru-issue` archive and attach a completed plan under), for additional context — and, if a documentation MCP (e.g. Confluence, Notion) is connected, searches it for pages relevant to the ticket or codebase for extra context. Use for onboarding, understanding "what would it take to fix issue #N"/"ticket PROJ-123", or getting oriented before planning work. For UI projects it also scans existing code for accessibility / assistive-technology support and reports an `Accessibility: present|partial|absent` line (with the `.ui-quality.yml` level, including `none`). Its "Tech stack" and "Related past implementation plans" findings (languages/frameworks, Antora docs location, repository host, relevant archived plans) are meant to be reused by later skills in the same conversation (e.g. `iru-plan`, `iru-code`, `iru-update-docs`, code review, branch/PR creation) to pick language/framework-appropriate flows, best practices, the right git-platform tooling, and proven prior plan structure.
